text:
lina: FYI I'm finalizing the new runtime/infra metrics dashboard (latency p50/p95/p99, token throughput, KV cache hitrate, request queue depth). Need to lock alert thresholds + pager routing before we flip the console rollout tomorrow morning. Who wants to own thresholds?

omar: i'd like to own the prometheus rules. question: do we page on p95 or p99 for latency? and do we prefer SLO-burn based alerts?

james: SLO-burn first. latency-only pages are noisy unless they're tied to error budget usage. propose burn-rate over 1h: >3 -> SEV0, >2 -> SEV1, >1.5 -> SEV2 (with some volume gating). p99-only for immediate latency flappers as a fallback for severe regressions.

tess: ops note: that mapping will produce a lot of alerts if we don't gate by QPS. suggest we require that the rolling 5m QPS > 50 before paging for SEV1/SEV0. For SEV2 let QPS > 20. Also non-prod clusters should be warn-only.

simone: also add KV cache health: hit_rate < 0.6 for >10m -> SEV2, <0.4 for 5m -> SEV1. request_queue_depth > 1000 for 5m -> SEV1 (this correlates tightly with latency).

lina: good catches. i want explicit thresholds in the dashboard UI so PMs can see the breakpoints. also need quotas alerts: per-customer token rate > 2x committed burst -> alert to billing/support (no page).

omar: drafting sample prometheus rules below — please review.

omar: ```yaml
- alert: Runtime_SLO_Burn_High
  expr: |
    (sum(rate(slo_error_budget_used_total[1h])) by (service) / sum(slo_error_budget_total) by (service)) > 2
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: pageable
    team: runtime
  annotations:
    summary: "Runtime SLO burn-rate >2 for {{ $labels.service }}"
    runbook: "https://confluence.redwood.local/runbooks/runtime-high-burn"
- alert: Runtime_P99_Latency_Spike
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) > 1.2
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: pageable
    team: runtime
  annotations:
    summary: "P99 latency > 1.2s for {{ $labels.service }}"
```

james: small nit: use error_budget_used_total normalized to the SLO window, and compute burn-rate properly. Also add volume gating: and(COUNT(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (service) > 50).

tess: for pager mapping: propose this mapping — SEV0/SEV1 -> eng-oncall (runtime rotation), SEV2 -> infra rotation (lead), SEV3/warn -> slack #runtime-alerts (no page). escalation: 5m -> secondary -> 10m -> platform-engineering manager.

simone: please include the KV cache + queue panels on top row and add an 'explain' panel for the burn-rate formula. helps triage.

lina: agree. also update the console rollout UX to show default threshold presets ("conservative", "balanced", "aggressive") so teams can opt-in. default should be "balanced" which uses the mapping above.

omar: i'll open the PR with the alert rules and the gating logic tonight. tagging @tess for PD/escalation changes.

tess: i'll update PagerDuty services and escalation policy. will create a PD service named runtime-high-burn and add the runtime oncall rotation. will also add a suppression rule for non-prod clusters.

pagerduty-bot: Created service runtime-high-burn and escalation policy "Runtime Oncall". https://redwood.pagerduty.com/services/P123456

james: runbook link please in annotations — make sure it contains: quick checks, dashboards to look at, safe rollback steps, and a script to restart the pool.

simone: i'll add the runbook section and link the KV cache remediation play.

lina: action list: Omar -> PR for prometheus rules (due EOD), Tess -> PD + rotation updates (EOD), Simone -> dashboard panels + runbook links (tomorrow morning), James -> update console rollout docs with threshold presets (tomorrow). anyone oppose?

james: lgtm :thumbsup:

omar: on it.

tess: ack, will update rotations.

simone: ack, starting dashboard work.

lina: thanks everyone. once PR merges i'll flip the rollout flag and we'll monitor burn-rate for 2 hours and iterate. :rocket:
